findings.text: the escalated route writes the selection only on the MAPPING_CANDIDATE edge (select_candidate, plan §8 map-context-reads-candidates) while the source's candidate_route stays 'escalated' from write_candidates, so count_candidates_by_route (imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:653), imas map status (imas_codex/cli/map.py:730) and discover status (imas_codex/cli/discover/__init__.py:161) will keep reporting a source that the model has since resolved as 'escalated', and the map claim keys on the edge flag while every status surface keys on the node property — two owners of one state that drift

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_codex/ids/candidates.py hides retrieval, arm merge/dedup, judgment templating and routing behind retrieve_candidates/route_ids/judge_candidates/route, and the candidate-edge read/write/clear stay co-located in graph_ops.py rather than spreading across the callers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan leaves two owners of "the selected candidate": the node property candidate_route (written by write_candidates, read by count_candidates_by_route) and the boolean route flag on the MAPPING_CANDIDATE edge (written by select_candidate), and an escalated pick updates only the edge.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §8 adds read_candidates/select_candidate and a TargetType classmethod but names what each surface retires or merges — imas map run loses --skip-metadata and --skip-errors, SignalSource loses mapping_target_ids/path/type, count_sources_by_mapping_status is deleted, the workers.py count_candidates_by_route copy is deleted, and the imas_node_embedding arm plus its post-hoc filter (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:681–694) are removed.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the machinery it builds on (hybrid_dd_search in imas_codex/graph/dd_search.py, call_decisions in imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3429, the generalised claim_batch in imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py:255, write_candidates/clear_candidates in imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py) and its MAPS_TO_IMAS writer census is verified accurate — both named greps now print only imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:585 (the MERGE) and :640 (the DELETE).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only wrapper-shaped addition, select_candidate, is explicitly justified against write_candidates' delete-and-rewrite semantics, so it is a distinct operation rather than a thin forwarder.
